subject: microbiology
title: Ophthalmia Neonatorum, Gonococcal PID and Moraxella catarrhalis

steps.tx: **Ophthalmia neonatorum** is conjunctivitis in the first month with a timetable of causes: chemical (first day, prophylaxis irritation), gonococcal (days 2 to 5, hyperpurulent, corneal ulcer and perforation risk), chlamydial inclusion (days 5 to 14, later pneumonia), herpetic and other bacteria. Gonococcal disease is an emergency of irrigation, systemic ceftriaxone, maternal and partner treatment and notification.
steps.say: Day two pus that threatens cornea is gonococcus until excluded; irrigate and treat systemically.

left.title: Timing table
points: Weeks 2 to 4: herpes and others by signs

right.title: Gonococcal eye response
points: Gram stain and NAAT and culture
Mother and partners evaluated and treated

steps.tx: **Ophthalmia neonatorum** is conjunctivitis in the first month, timed by cause. Chemical irritation from prophylaxis appears on the first day. Gonococcal disease arrives around days two to five, hyperpurulent, and can ulcerate or perforate the cornea. Chlamydial inclusion conjunctivitis appears around days five to fourteen and may be followed by pneumonia. Herpes and other bacteria also occur. Gonococcal disease needs irrigation, systemic ceftriaxone, treatment of mother and partner, and notification.
steps.say: Conjunctivitis in the first month follows a timetable: chemical on day one, gonococcus around days two to five with pus that threatens the cornea, chlamydia later and sometimes pneumonia. Gonococcal disease needs irrigation, systemic ceftriaxone, partner treatment, and notification.

vis.alt: A newborn eye is swollen shut and pouring thick yellow pus.
vis.caption: A newborn eyelid is tense with hyperpurulent discharge, the emergency face of gonococcal ophthalmia. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Prophylaxis traditions** (Crede silver nitrate historical, erythromycin ointment, povidone iodine in trials) protect where maternal screening gaps persist, their value debated where antenatal STI care is universal. Prevention here is obstetric microbiology applied to a newborn's first hour. Where mothers receive documented gonorrhoea and chlamydia screening with treatment, several guidelines allow selective prophylaxis, but the ointment remains cheap insurance in uncertain histories.
steps.say: Eye prophylaxis insures against unscreened births; screening is the fairer policy.

left.title: Prophylaxis agents
points: Silver nitrate 1 percent historical chemical conjunctivitis

right.title: Policy divides
points: Screening based systems omit routine ointment
Chlamydia not prevented by ocular prophylaxis

steps.tx: **Pelvic inflammatory disease** ascends from cervix (gonococcus and chlamydia principals, anaerobes and mycoplasmas joining) to endometritis, salpingitis, tubo ovarian abscess and perihepatitis (Fitz Hugh Curtis), costing fertility and ectopic risk per episode, treated broadly and early on clinical suspicion (cervical motion tenderness) without awaiting NAAT, partners treated and retesting scheduled.
steps.say: Treat PID on suspicion tonight; tubes scar while cultures deliberate.

left.title: PID portrait
points: Fever in moderate severe, silent salpingitis exists
Risk: youth, new partners, prior PID

right.title: PID management
points: Ceftriaxone plus doxycycline plus metronidazole traditions
Pregnancy test and HIV syphilis screening
Partner treatment and abstinence until complete

steps.tx: **Pelvic inflammatory disease** climbs from the cervix, with gonococcus and chlamydia as the main agents and anaerobes and mycoplasmas joining later. It becomes endometritis, salpingitis, tubo ovarian abscess, and perihepatitis known as Fitz Hugh Curtis disease, the violin string adhesions on the liver. Each episode costs fertility and raises ectopic risk. Treatment is broad and starts on clinical suspicion, including cervical motion tenderness, without waiting for nucleic acid tests. Partners are treated and retesting is scheduled.
steps.say: Gonococcus and chlamydia ascend from the cervix to endometrium, tubes, abscess, and perihepatitis with violin string liver adhesions. Fertility falls with each episode. Treat on cervical motion tenderness the same day, cover partners, and plan retesting. Do not wait for nucleic acid results.

vis.alt: A laparoscopic view of the liver shows fine violin string adhesions between the capsule and the abdominal wall.
vis.caption: Fine violin string adhesions stretch from the liver capsule, the laparoscopic mark of perihepatitis. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Disseminated gonococcal infection** (arthritis dermatitis syndrome) seeds blood to tenosynovitis, pustular skin lesions and migratory pain, or settles as purulent single joint arthritis, cultures often negative from joints but NAAT and mucosal sites positive, complement deficiency in recurrence, ceftriaxone therapy until improvement then oral by susceptibility.
steps.say: Tenosynovitis, pustules and a wandering joint: culture the cervix when the knee is silent.

steps.tx: **Moraxella catarrhalis** completes the Neisseria neighbourhood: gram negative diplococcus, oxidase and DNase positive, tributyrin positive, hockey puck colonies sliding intact, causing otitis media, sinusitis and COPD exacerbations (third bacterial author), with BRO beta lactamases in over 90 percent making amoxicillin unreliable, vaccines elusive by surface variation.
steps.say: Hockey puck colonies and universal beta lactamase: Moraxella in COPD sputum is rarely innocent.

right.title: Moraxella disease
points: Amoxicillin clavulanate and successors by susceptibility

steps.tx: **Pharyngeal gonorrhoea** hides as the resistance incubator: mostly asymptomatic, harder to eradicate, culture and test of cure traditions strongest here, NAAT validated per site, implicated in resistance selection by suboptimal exposure and commensal gene exchange (mosaic penA ancestors in commensal Neisseria).
steps.say: The throat hides gonococcus, shelters resistance genes and demands test of cure.

left.title: Pharyngeal facts
points: Usually asymptomatic, screening by exposure history
NAAT positive needs culture attempts in failure
Test of cure at 7 to 14 days traditions

steps.tx: **Neonatal chlamydial disease** pairs with gonococcal in this lesson because prophylaxis separates them: inclusion conjunctivitis days 5 to 14 (watery to mucopurulent, no corneal panic) and afebrile pneumonia with staccato cough at 4 to 12 weeks, treated systemically (macrolide with pyloric stenosis counselling in young infants), mother and partners treated.
steps.say: Week two conjunctivitis, month two staccato cough: chlamydia's neonatal timetable.

left.title: Chlamydial eye
points: Onset 5 to 14 days, lid swelling and discharge

right.title: Chlamydial pneumonia
points: Macrolide systemic therapy, erythromycin pyloric caution

steps.tx: **Partner and public health obligations** in gonococcal disease (expedited partner therapy where legal, 60 day lookback, retest for reinfection at three months, HIV PrEP offers, syphilis and hepatitis screening) are microbiology delivered by clinic systems; cure without partner therapy is reinfection scheduled.
steps.say: Treat partners and retest at three months, or meet the same infection again.

left.title: Partner work
points: Test of cure in pregnancy and pharynx

right.title: Reinfection logic
points: Retest at 3 months (not test of cure confusion)
HIV and syphilis incidence high in cohorts
PrEP and vaccination offers (hepatitis, HPV, mpox by risk)
